candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 25 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 26 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 27 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 28 not required. 29
candidates.context: This guidance is intended to assist applicants requesting New Clinical Investigation exclusivity 16 (also referred to as 3-year exclusivity) for a new drug application (NDA) or NDA supplement 17 under sections 505(c)(3)(E)(iii)-(iv) and 505(j)(5)(F)(iii)-(iv) of the Federal Food, Drug, and 18 Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). The guidance discusses the statutory and regulatory criteria for 19 eligibility for New Clinical Investigation exclusivity and provides recommendations on the 20 content and format of requests for New Clinical Investigation exclusivity in the form of 21 questions and answers (Q&As). FDA intends to update this draft guidance document to include 22 additional Q&As as appropriate. 23

candidates.statement: The Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act of 1984 (Public Law 98-417) 34 (Hatch-Waxman Amendments), which added sections 505(b)(2) and 505(j) to the FD&C Act (21 35 U.S.C. sections 355(b)(2) and 355(j)), reflects Congress’s efforts to balance the need to “make 36 available more low cost generic drugs by establishing a generic drug approval procedure” with 37 new incentives for drug development in the form of exclusivities and patent term extensions. 2

candidates.statement: QB.2. Does the drug used in the clinical investigation need to be the same as that 123 approved for the application to qualify for 3-year exclusivity? 124
candidates.context: FDA’s regulations implementing the Hatch-Waxman exclusivity provisions define a 119 clinical investigation as “any experiment other than a bioavailability study in which a 120 drug is administered or dispensed to, or used on, human subjects.” 11,12 FDA does not require the drug used in the clinical investigation to be the same as that 126 approved for the application to qualify for 3-year exclusivity provided that all 127 requirements of 21 CFR § 314.108 and section 505(c)(3)(E)(iii) or (iv) of the FD&C Act 128 are met. For example, a clinical investigation that used a similar or earlier version of the 129 drug product in development, which contains the same active moiety or combination of 130 active moieties as the version of the drug in the approved application, may potentially 131 qualify the approved drug product for 3-year exclusivity. candidates.statement: To show that the NDA contains new clinical investigations, the applicant must include a 213 certification that to the best of its knowledge: (1) each of the clinical investigations is an 214 investigation in humans; (2) the results of which have not been relied on by FDA to 215 demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness of a previously approved drug product 216 for any indication or of safety for a new patient population; and (3) do not duplicate the 217 results of another investigation that was relied on by the Agency to demonstrate the 218 effectiveness or safety in a new patient population of a previously approved drug 219 product 21 (see QE.1 on the process for requesting 3-year exclusivity). In the past, 220 supportive information for the certification has included a statement indicating that the 221 study results have never been previously submitted to FDA; a list of other applications 222 for which the results of the clinical investigation may have been previously submitted but 223 not relied on for substantial evidence of effectiveness or safety for a new patient 224 population of a previously approved drug product; or an explanation of how the clinical 225 investigation differs from another investigation previously relied on by the Agency for 226 effectiveness or safety for a new patient population of a previously approved drug 227 product. FDA will evaluate the information submitted by the applicant, and the Agency 228 will determine whether the NDA contains “new clinical investigations” under the statute 229 and regulations. 230

FDA’s approach incentivizes 275 sponsors to submit results from distinct cohorts or treatment arms as soon as they are 276 available, resulting in approval of corresponding information in drug labeling more 277 quickly. candidates.statement: To meet this standard, the clinical investigation must be “vital” to the application and 300 there must not be any published studies (other than the applicant’s) or other information 301 available to FDA that would allow the Agency to approve the proposed drug product for 302 the proposed conditions of use or the change to the already approved drug product. 29 In 303 other words, without the new clinical investigation, FDA would not have sufficient 304 information to conclude that the drug product or change to the approved drug product for 305 which the applicant is seeking approval is safe and effective. candidates.statement: An investigation is conducted or sponsored by the applicant if “before or during the 341 investigation, the applicant was named in Form FDA-1571 filed with FDA as the sponsor 342 of the investigational new drug [IND] application under which the investigation was 343 conducted, or the applicant or the applicant’s predecessor in interest, provided substantial 344 support for the investigation.” 35 A predecessor in interest is an entity, e.g., a corporation, 345 that the applicant has taken over, merged with, or purchased, or from which the applicant 346 has purchased all rights to the drug. 36 QD.2 addresses how an applicant must show that it 347 conducted or sponsored a new clinical investigation. 348
